text:
maya: Heads up — after the staged rate-limit cutover (policy ps-202) we started seeing 429s and elevated tail latency for a handful of hosted customers. Noticed spikes at 14:05 UTC.
liam: Thanks — which customers and any request ids / headers you can share? Did the deploybot show rollout %s?
deploybot: rollout started ps-202 -> cohort=staged-cutover-030, start=2026-03-17T14:02:10Z, target=10% traffic.
maya: acme-inc and two smaller partners. Example response from 14:06: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: rq_0a9f12
x-rate-limit-policy: ps-202
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
Retry-After: 30
```
curl we used to repro: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}'`
sam: Are those customers on legacy quotas or the new per-app rate? We didn't change committed reserved buckets for Dedicated.
maya: Hosted, not dedicated. They were part of the 10% cohort by rollout tag.
jordan: Can we pull rate-limiter logs for ps-202 across edge nodes? Sounds like backpressure where a hot client triggers per-key exhaustion and upstream queues spiking. Also check auth-retry loops — some clients retry aggressively.
liam: Quick mitigation options: 1) rollback cohort to ps-201 (previous policy) 2) temporarily increase burst window for affected cohort 3) enable client-specified Retry-After enforcement at edge to reduce retry storms. Which is fastest?
jordan: Rollback is fastest for safety. We can revert cohort config via control-plane with near-zero downtime. I'll prepare the rollback play.
maya: Please note acme-inc is in the middle of billing reconciliation today — let's coordinate messaging before any change that affects usage.
rebecca: I'll ping the customer immediately and say we're investigating and may do a temporary policy revert; will offer timeline.
liam: Plan: 14:18 UTC — initiate rollback for cohort=staged-cutover-030 -> ps-201. 14:20 UTC — monitor 429 rate and p95 latency. Jordan to run quick limiter log query: `grep ps-202 /var/log/ratelimiter/* | tail -n 200` and paste top offending keys.
platform-bot: rollback initiated -> cohort=staged-cutover-030, target=ps-201, action_id=rb_20260317_01, status=in-progress
jordan: Found concentrated traffic from client_key=acme-service-1, 87% of 429s. Looks like client isn't honoring Retry-After and has tight retry loops. Will add a temporary bypass for acme-service-1 to reduce hard failures while CS engages the customer.
sam: If bypass, we should also throttle at edge with exponential backoff headers to avoid downstream overload.
liam: Agreed. Jordan, proceed with rollback + temporary bypass and add edge backoff header. Maya/Rebecca, keep customer updated. After rollback and 10m of stable metrics we can re-evaluate a smaller staged rollout with adjusted burst windows.
maya: Got it — will update acme-inc now.
platform-bot: rollback completed -> action_id=rb_20260317_01, status=success, completed_at=2026-03-17T14:23:05Z
jordan: Post-rollback checks: 429s dropped to baseline in 5 minutes, p95 latency improved. Offending client still doing tight retries; CS to notify them to add jitter/backoff.
rebecca: Message sent to acme-inc. They acknowledged and will patch their client to honor Retry-After and add jitter.
liam: Follow-ups: (1) adjust default burst window for future rollouts, (2) add a preflight regression check that detects hot-key concentration, (3) add an automated temporary-bypass playbook for known business-critical customers.
maya: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
